-- Fifth domain concept: a note is a free-text remark the user jots against something. It is written
-- generically against a target (target_type + target_id) rather than a single FK, so the same notes
-- surface can later sit on any entity (projects today). IDENTITY id so the app generates ids on
-- create, while the test seed inserts explicit ids (GENERATED BY DEFAULT lets a supplied id win).
-- created_at is when the note was written — the newest-first ordering the UI shows is by this column
-- (DESC), with the id as a stable tie-break. New rows default to now(); the test seed supplies an
-- explicit timestamp so a fixture can pin the order.
CREATE TABLE notes (
    id          BIGINT GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    target_type VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL,
    target_id   BIGINT NOT NULL,
    text        VARCHAR(4000) NOT NULL,
    created_at  TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

-- The detail page reads one target's notes newest-first, so index the lookup + ordering columns.
CREATE INDEX idx_notes_target ON notes (target_type, target_id, created_at DESC);

# The agent's test loop (DESIGN.md §15): build, start the whole app, run ONLY the specs currently

export BASE_URL="http://localhost:${PORT}"
# Known audit file, shared by the app (bin/start) and the specs (support/audit.ts). Absolute.

bin/build
bin/start
cleanup() { bin/stop || true; }

## Summary

The change request — "add notes to invoices too, not just jobs" — is implemented as a small, additive, full-stack change.

The key finding: the notes system was **already generic**. The `notes` table keys on `(target_type, target_id)`, the REST endpoints (`GET`/`POST /api/notes`) take `targetType`/`targetId` with no whitelist, and the project notes panel just hardcodes `targetType='project'`. So no schema migration or server-logic change was needed for invoice notes to work — adding one would have been dead weight.

What I actually changed:

1. **Front-end — new slot panel** `src/main/frontend/features/invoices/notes.slot.tsx`: an `InvoiceDetail.fill(...)` contribution rendering `data-testid="invoice-notes"`, the newest-first list (`note-row-<id>` / `note-text`), and the add form (`note-form-text` / `note-form-submit`) — mirroring the project panel but scoped to `targetType='invoice'`. Per the "features never import each other" rule, it has its own tiny client `src/main/frontend/features/invoices/notesApi.ts` that stays in step with any other notes surface by sharing the query key `['notes', targetType, targetId]` (list reads it, add form invalidates it).

2. **Seed support fix** in `TestSupportController.java`: the test fixture pins a note's `at` as a plain date (`'2026-02-01'`), which `OffsetDateTime.parse` rejects. I made the parse fall back to interpreting a date-only value as start-of-day UTC, so the newest-first ordering stays deterministic. This is the app-owned, schema-evolving seed path (not pinned), so editing it is in bounds.

`bin/e2e` passes (`1 passed`) and `npm run typecheck` is clean. No pinned scaffolding or the spec was touched.

The exploration report confirms my implementation matches the established pattern exactly — and I'd already handled the one subtlety it didn't flag: the seed's `at` parsing rejecting the test's date-only `'2026-02-01'`.

The change is complete and verified. Nothing further is needed:

- **New frontend slot** `features/invoices/notes.slot.tsx` filling `InvoiceDetail` (`invoice.detail`) with `targetType='invoice'` and the exact testids the spec asserts (`invoice-notes`, `note-row-<id>`, `note-text`, `note-form-text`, `note-form-submit`) — auto-registered by slot discovery, no existing file edited.
- **New** `features/invoices/notesApi.ts`, self-contained per the "features never import each other" rule, sharing the `['notes', targetType, targetId]` query key so the cache stays consistent.
- **Seed fix** in `TestSupportController.java` so a date-only `at` is accepted (start-of-day UTC).
- **No migration or server-logic change** — the `notes` table and the `/api/notes` endpoints are already generic over `targetType`, so forcing a new migration would have been dead weight against the "small, additive, local" guidance.

`bin/e2e` → `1 passed`; `npm run typecheck` → clean.
